clue.text: Both taps drip — see variable pressure

parts.note: a pair of taps is marked C for cold and H for hot
a hospital drip is an intravenous line, IV
v. is short for vide, Latin for 'see'
algebra's unknowns and variables are x, y and z

explanation.surface: A plumber notices that both taps drip and blames fluctuating water pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To chivvy is to nag or hurry someone along, which is to put pressure on them.

clue.text: Beat it with very famous investor

parts.note: to cap is to beat or outdo
taken as written
A-list describes top celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone tries to outdo a celebrity financier at investing.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalist is a person who puts private money into business for profit, an investor.

clue.text: Edition is, of course, not right

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: saying a word is not something means that element is taken out of it

parts.note: 'of course!' and 'sure!' both mean certainly
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a particular edition of a book is, naturally, the wrong one.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a magazine or newspaper is one edition of it, published at a particular time.

clue.text: Promoter of the other version of Sex & The City?

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, and the Roman version of six is VI
Agra, home of the Taj Mahal, is a city in India

explanation.surface: A wry question about what would boost a racier remake of the TV show Sex and the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is a British euphemism for sex, so its promoter is the impotence drug. The famous show title has to be split: Sex is read as Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The impotence drug is taken to make sex possible, so it is a promoter of 'the other', a coy British term for sex.

clue.text: Dog meat 50% part of take-away food

parts.note: the chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: fifty per cent means only half of the word is kept, here its first two letters

parts.note: the first half of the four-letter word
to be in something is to be part of it

explanation.surface: A grim rumour that dog meat makes up half of a Chinese takeaway dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the old slur about Chinese takeaways; the dog is in fact a Chinese breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein, fried noodles with meat and vegetables, is a staple dish of Chinese takeaway restaurants.

clue.text: Embassy's expensive fee

parts.note: a high price is an expensive one
a commission is a fee paid to an agent

explanation.surface: Complaining that an embassy charges a steep fee for its services.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A high commission is the embassy one Commonwealth country keeps in another, headed by a high commissioner.

clue.text: Make-up — defect is not commonly seen

parts.note: a warp is a twist or flaw, as in timber
ain't is the colloquial form of 'is not'

explanation.surface: A cosmetics advert promising its make-up hides a blemish completely.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is the face paint warriors wore, and jokingly any heavy cosmetics.

clue.text: One explains old model with skimpy clothing

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: the model is placed with clothing around it, so one word is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: skimpy means poor or meagre; clothing is the wrapper
to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: Someone justifies an elderly model's revealing outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' looks like the noun for garments, but it is the verb: the meagre word dresses the model.
explanation.definitionFit: An expositor sets out and interprets a text or idea, so is a person who explains.

clue.text: To be a jogger's no good without kit

indicators.note: 'no good' means the letter for good is to be left out

parts.note: to nudge someone is to jog them, so it is what a jogger does
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark that running in the buff does a jogger no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The jogger is not a runner but one who jogs an elbow; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nude has no clothes on at all, so is without kit, British slang for clothing.

clue.text: Not to be justified on earth? How appropriate

parts.note: to go forth is to go on
E is the abbreviation for Earth
'How!' is the greeting associated with Native Americans in westerns
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that an unjustifiable act on Earth is somehow fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'how on earth' is broken up: on and earth go together, and How is a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for the hell of it means doing it for no reason at all, so it cannot be justified.

clue.text: Old man's shop beginning to go forward

parts.note: pa is a dad, an old man, with the possessive s
a salon is a shop such as a hairdresser's

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Dad's shop is starting to make progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' reads like an adverb of movement, but it is the verb for sending a letter on.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass along a message or parcel is to forward it to the next person.

clue.text: Fleet's power in attack

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside that word

parts.note: a raid is a surprise attack
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A naval fleet's might is shown when it attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a navy but is the adjective for swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift or quick on one's feet, the same as rapid.

clue.text: Scholars notice earth is round?

indicators.note: to bring letters round is to turn them about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Academics observe that the world is a globe, phrased as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' reads as the shape of the planet, which is just what theorists worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoreticians work out abstract principles rather than practice, like scholars in their studies.

clue.text: Education through acquisition, of course

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, relating to a set course of action

indicators.note: running through another word means sitting inside it

parts.note: procural is a rare word for procurement, acquiring something
ED is the abbreviation for education

explanation.surface: Learning comes through acquiring knowledge, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally', but it is the definition: a course here is a process.
explanation.definitionFit: Procedural means relating to procedure, an established course of steps to be followed.

clue.text: Cat left in part of hotel

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
in a role is acting as it

indicators.note: taking a part of a word means keeping only a piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A cat has been left behind somewhere in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, not a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails is a multi-thonged whip, and a lash is a whip or its stroke.

clue.text: Tack into wind and run this sail

indicators.note: one word going into another is placed inside it

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a path does
a tack is a small pin
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Sailing instructions: tack into the wind, then run with this sail up.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack, wind and run all look like sailing terms, which suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is the large balloon-shaped sail set at the front of a yacht for running downwind.

clue.text: Dressmaker keeps touching fabulous swimmer

indicators.note: a word that keeps another holds it inside itself

parts.note: a seamster sews clothes
on can mean touching, resting against

explanation.surface: A dressmaker keeps handling a wonderful swimmer, perhaps a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means belonging to fable, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea monster is a creature of legend and fable that swims in the ocean.

clue.text: Queen needs him to carry the odd crown? No

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside

parts.note: a queen bee needs a male drone to mate with

indicators.note: something odd is strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A queen asks whether her consort must bear the strange crown, and is refused.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen is a bee, not a monarch. 'Crown? No' means the opposite of crowning.
explanation.definitionFit: To dethrone a monarch is to remove them from power, the reverse of crowning them.

clue.text: Unique, troubled genius rejected father

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so its letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A tormented one-of-a-kind genius disowned his father.
explanation.definitionFit: Sui generis is Latin for 'of its own kind', describing something unique that fits no category.

clue.text: Tailless bird caught small reptile

indicators.note: without a tail, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a crow is a black bird
c. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail has caught a little lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals a shortened word: the reptile is the crocodile, cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the clipped, informal form of crocodile, so a reptile name made small.

clue.text: Arrangement of bones makes us look bad?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of bones in the skeleton
second meaning, cryptic: split into two words, it says someone blackens our name

explanation.surface: Someone worries whether the layout of a skeleton display reflects poorly on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as TARS US, the answer reads as a verb phrase: to tar someone is to smear their reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsus is the group of seven bones forming the ankle and back of the foot.

clue.text: Fully open, as any lock can be picked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unrestrained, with no limits

definitions.text: as any lock can be picked
definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: in wrestling a lock is a hold, and if none is banned the wrestler may choose any

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' and 'picked' suggest a burglar; in wrestling a lock is a grip that pins the opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from wrestling bouts where no grip was banned, and now means unrestrained in any contest.

clue.text: Put up and knock down, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word goes by its sound

parts.note: to raze a building is to knock it down

explanation.surface: A builder's contradictory instructions to erect and demolish something.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are opposites in meaning but identical in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a building or flag is to put it up, set it upright.

clue.text: Extremely short work break

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
op. is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An office worker gets a very brief rest from their job.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a pause or halt in a journey or activity, the same as a break.

clue.text: Destination Kentucky's old capital

parts.note: to marks where something is headed
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A traveller names the former capital of Kentucky as their destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old capital' looks like one phrase, but old stands alone and capital is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: More stale works of writers

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, reshaped like raw material

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A critic says some authors' books are getting more tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as books but is the verb that reshapes the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowsty means stuffy and stale-smelling, as a shut-up room is; this is its comparative.

clue.text: Makes textbook for a following — weird sect

parts.note: per means for each, as in so much per head

indicators.note: something weird is strange and out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strange cult writes a manual for its followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a cult's band of believers, but it is just the abbreviation f.
explanation.definitionFit: Textbook as an adjective means exemplary, so to make something textbook is to make it perfect.

clue.text: Ordinary bag of bones

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
to bag something is informally to take or steal it

explanation.surface: Just an ordinary skinny person, a bag of bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag of bones' wants to be one phrase; bag is the verb and 'of bones' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is an adjective meaning relating to or like bone, from the Greek for bone.
